Aditya / Neha — drafting answers below that we can send to MedSync. I attached the SOC 2 report stub and a short KMS overview for their review.

Attachments: SOC2-Report-2025.pdf, KMS-Overview-Redwood.pdf

Short answers to Olivia's KMS questions (for insertion into the questionnaire):

1) Encryption in transit and at rest
- In transit: All network traffic to/from Redwood endpoints is encrypted using TLS 1.2+; TLS 1.3 is enabled on public endpoints.
- At rest: Data stored by Redwood (customer data, artifacts, logs where applicable) is encrypted using AES-256. Persistent model checkpoints and cache blobs are encrypted at rest.

2) Key storage and access controls
- Default keys: Redwood-managed (stored in cloud KMS providers) with strict RBAC and separation of duties. Access to key material by Redwood personnel is audited and restricted to the minimum required by operations.
- Customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK): Customers can supply keys via their cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault). Keys are used in an envelope encryption pattern where data keys are generated per-customer and encrypted with the customer key. Redwood does not persist plaintext customer master keys.

3) HSM support & FIPS
- We support HSM-backed KMS providers (AWS CloudHSM integrations via KMS, Google Cloud HSM, and Azure Dedicated HSM). For customers requiring on-prem HSMs, we offer solution patterns (e.g., proxy KMS) as part of our Private deployment options.

4) Key rotation
- Customers can rotate CMKs on their schedule; rotation is supported via the underlying KMS. For Redwood-managed keys we perform rotation per industry best practices and notify customers in advance for major changes. Envelope keys (data keys) are rotated per-configurable TTLs.

5) Logging & attestation
- All key usage and KMS API calls are logged (CloudTrail / equivalent) and available for audit export. SOC 2 report and our security team can provide attestation details.

6) BAA and HIPAA
- We will sign a BAA for HIPAA-covered use. SOC 2 Type II report is attached as requested — redacted version for vendor consumption. For PHI workloads we recommend a Private instance or Dedicated capacity with CMEK enabled; we can walk through architecture during the call.

Recommendation: send the attached SOC2-Report-2025.pdf and KMS-Overview-Redwood.pdf back to Olivia, confirm whether they want us to complete the questionnaire in-line or via a quick collaborative session. Suggest a 30-min call (Neha + Marissa) Wed/Thu next week 9:00-11:30 PST.
